text: The is a weapon attachment featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, Call of Duty: Black Ops II, Call of Duty Online, Call of Duty: Ghosts, Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare, Call of Duty: WWII and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 Campaign Remastered for handguns. It is also available in Call of Duty: Black Ops: Declassified for other weapons as well. It was also cut from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered.

Tank War is a cut gametype from Call of Duty: World at War. Little is known about it, being the only thing that proves its existence is audio files of the announcers, and a file that appeared for it in the records section in the beta. According to the name, and the voices from the announcers the gametype was going to be based around armored warfare. Similar to regular Team Deathmatch, the goal would have most likely been to destroy as many enemy tanks as possible. It would have most likely been the Japanese Type 97 tanks vs. the American M4 Sherman tanks, and the Russian T-34 vs. the German Panzer IV. That would mean the Type 97 and the M4 Sherman could have been added to multiplayer.
The TOW (Tube-Launched, Optically-Tracked, Wire Command Data Link, guided missile) is an anti-tank missile system first used by the United States Military during the Vietnam War.

The T-55 appears as the main battle tank of the North Vietnamese Army in the campaign and as a power-up in the Dead Ops Arcade map, Dead Ops Arcade, as well as being a prop in the Multiplayer of Call of Duty: Black Ops. It then appears in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare as a prop, and in Call of Duty: Black Ops 6 where it is used by the Iraqi Armed Forces in the campaign.

A Tank Destroyer is an armored vehicle that was designed to take out other medium tanks. Most tank destroyers sported a powerful main gun and may have had one or more machine guns for defense. A tank destroyer has appeared in Call of Duty: United Offensive as both an objective to be destroyed in the campaign and a drivable vehicle in multiplayer. The tank destroyers that have appeared in the Call of Duty series are: *Elefant - The tank destroyer used by the Germans in Call of Duty: United Offensive. *SU-152 - The tank destroyer used by the Soviets in Call of Duty: United Offensive. *Nashorn - A tank destroyer that was cut from Call of Duty: World at War.
The T-90 is a main battle tank that appears in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 and Call of Duty: Ghosts. It was cut from Call of Duty: Black Ops II.

The is a Soviet main battle tank, a further development of the T-55, that appears in Call of Duty: Black Ops II. T-62s appear in the missions Pyrrhic Victory where they are used by the MPLA, and Old Wounds where a single tank is seen driving out of a Mujahideen bunker, and they are also used by Soviet troops to attack the Mujahideen compound, and in the strike mission I.E.D where they are used by Mujahideen. In Call of Duty: Black Ops 7, the T-62 is mentioned by Nikolai Belinski as being his "wife's name".

The is a small lightweight patrol boat that appears in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 as the Russian Navy's main fast-attack craft. It appears in the level Hunter Killer and pursues the player after escaping the Oscar-II submarine in a Zodiac.
The Targeting Drone is a vehicle featured in Call of Duty: Ghosts, in the mission "Loki", where it is used to designate targets for the LOKI Space Station.

The Tank Upgrade is a bonus pickup in Call of Duty: Ghosts in Chaos Mode, as well as a class upgrade that can be purchased for use in regular missions. Once picked-up and/or used, the player will become invincible for up to fifteen seconds (up to ten seconds outside of Chaos Mode). While the upgrade is active, all cryptids will redirect their focus to attack the player. While the upgrade is active, the player is able to stun cryptids with melee attacks. When active, the player's screen will be gray. Other players can see when someone else is using the upgrade as four red lines will constantly be pulsing around the player. This upgrade essentially turns the Tank player into a human Flare, fully diverting the attention of cryptids. The Tank upgrade is great to use in a pinch or when tackling tons of enemies that are within striking distance of the user. The upgrade can also be used when teammates are in trouble, diverting attention off of them and allowing them to perform their job more effectively. It can be perfect for when an ally needs a moment to retrieve something or fix the Laser Drill. The Tank Upgrade will not stop players from taking damage from falling off of the map, as this is an instakill. This will still cause the player to immediately bleed out and need to be revived from their Dog Tags, or in solo play, this will still count as a down and cost the player one of their lives. The Tank Upgrade will also not fully prevent Scorpion and Seeder acid. The Tank Upgrade
Tattoo Personalization Pack is a downloadable content package available for Call of Duty: Ghosts. It contains a weapon camo, reticle, a player background, and a player patch.
The T-740 Hovertank is a tank in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare.

The T-600 Titan is a heavy tank developed for the Armed Forces of the United States of America and the Atlas Corporation. The Main Battle tank has superior mobility compared to its traditional counterparts, as it has four vehicle treads that can double as legs in order to traverse rough terrain and avoid a variety of manmade or natural obstacles. Onboard offensive weapons constitute a smoothbore cannon, a machine gun turret and twin rocket launchers. Its defensive weapons include a trophy system, which intercepts any incoming projectiles headed for the vehicle.

, a common Support weapon in the Call of Duty series]] Support, in some cases referred to as Assault, is a class of automatic weapons featured in Call of Duty, Call of Duty: United Offensive, Call of Duty: Finest Hour, Call of Duty 2, Call of Duty 2: Big Red One, Call of Duty 3 and Call of Duty: Roads to Victory. In the later games of the series, support weapons are divided between Automatic rifles and machine guns.

The Sword is a melee weapon featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered, Call of Duty: Mobile, and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III. Swords are also briefly seen in Call of Duty: Black Ops III, and were going to be featured in the cut installment Call of Duty: Roman Wars.
Captain Taras Emin is a character who appears in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare and member of the Settlement Defense Front. He's assigned to the SetDef carrier Cerberus.

Tank Zombies are a unit in Call of Duty: Heroes, available in the Zombie Drop Pod. Tank Zombies are noticeably larger than Infector Zombies and Sniper Zombies. They have a large amount of health, and can only attack with a close range, smash attack; a unique ability available to Tank Zombies is that they are able to regenerate their health if damaged.

Supercell is an Epic gun perk in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. It is the EMC - Switchblade's exclusive trait, converting the gun from firing normal energy rounds to becoming a shot pistol, firing multiple pellets. It is deadly in close quarters, where the generous magazine size and damage really come into their own. It does reduce range, so mid range battles are practically impossible. However, it more than makes up for it in being an easy to use pistol at close quarters as well as packing a strong punch.

The Tactical EMP Launcher appears as an underbarrel attachment integrated to the Raijin-EMX submachine gun in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. It is a launcher that fires a small EMP device that creates a small EMP blast on impact, disabling player HUDs, Scorestreaks and Payloads that are in the blast radius.

Tactical Kit is an Epic gun perk in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. It is exclusive to the Epic Raijin-EMX - Synergy variant. The perk improves the effects of the underbarrel Tactical EMP Launcher, provides the weapon a unique sight, and also prevents the revealing of an enemies' death location to their teammates in a similar manner to the Assassin Build gun perk. It also converts the three-round burst submachine gun into a four-round burst submachine gun.

The Sword of Barbarossa is a mystical blade that was forged in ancient Thule. It would fall into the possession of German holy Emperor Frederick Barbarossa during the Third Crusade. Following Barbarossa's death, the sword was broken into pieces and scattered across Europe. During World War II, the sword pieces would be reclaimed from their resting places by the MFAA, who sought to use the sword to destroy the now uncontrollable undead forces. Bringing the sword pieces to Thule located in Antarctica, the MFAA were successful in forging the pieces together, thus restoring the sword to its original glory and full power.

The SwordFish is a four-round burst bullpup rifle appearing as a tactical rifle in Call of Duty: Black Ops 4, as an assault rifle in Call of Duty: Mobile, and as a marksman rifle in Call of Duty: Black Ops 7.
The Switchblade X9 is a submachine gun featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops 4 and Call of Duty: Mobile.

The Tactical Flashlight is a Signature Attachment for the RUS-79U submachine gun in Call of Duty: Mobile. It was added in May 2023 as part of the Season 5: Get Wrecked! update. Tapping the toggle button will toggle on the flashlight, which will emit the light that highlights the enemies at close range for 15.3s. The effect will become diminished greater the longer the distance between the user and the targets. The duration can be indicated by the toggle button, which begins to run out as long as the flashlight stays active. After 15.3s, the button and the flashlight will become disappeared and unusable, respectively.

The [https://military.polaris.com/en-us/mrzr-d4-military-tan/specs/ Tac Rover] is a ground vehicle featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare. It is available for use in Multiplayer in the Ground War mode. The Tac Rover is also available in Call of Duty: Warzone.
Tank Battle is a game type for the Battle Royale mode of Call of Duty: Mobile, introduced as part of Season 2: Day of Reckoning.
The is a straight pull bolt-action sniper rifle featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War. It was added as part of the Season Three update.

The is a weapon that appears as a submachine gun in Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War and Call of Duty: Mobile, and as a fully-automatic handgun in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III.

The T1 Flash Hider is a Muzzle Attachment available in Call of Duty: Vanguard. It helps to reduces the amount of muzzle flash created from the gun and reduces recoil at the cost of the aim down sight speed.

The TLL Disk Trim is a Muzzle attachment available uniquely for the EX1 Assault Rifle in Call of Duty: Vanguard. It helps to increase the damage range, recoil control and accuracy but at the cost of the damage.
Tactique Verte, sometimes called Tactique Verte Inc., abbreviated as TV or TAQ, is a weapon manufacturer in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III.

The TAV, also known as the Tactical Amphibious Vehicle, is an amphibious vehicle featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II and Call of Duty: Warzone 2.0. It was added as part of the Season Four update. The TAV allows players to traverse through land and through water. The TAV appears as a static prop in Call of Duty: Mobile.

The is a bullpup assault rifle featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II. It was added as part of the Season Six update. The TR-76 Geist is also available in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III as part of the Modern Warfare II content carryover.
The is a light machine gun featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III. It was added on January 17th, 2024 as part of the Season One Reloaded update.

The Tactical Bike is a vehicle featured in the Blackout mode of Call of Duty: Black Ops 4. The Tactical Bike was added with the Operation Apocalypse Z update. The bike can sit up to two people, the driver and a passenger on the side car.
The is a submachine gun featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III. It was added as part of the Season Four update.
The is a submachine gun featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops 6.
TOS is a weapon manufacturer in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III.

The Tactical Laser is an attachment in Call of Duty: Black Ops 6. It is categorised under the Laser category. It allows the weapon to go into the Tactical Stance for balance of mobility and accuracy, at the cost of the visible laser whilst in the stance.
The Tactical Foregrip B is an underbarrel attachment featured in Call of Duty: Mobile, available to the AK117 assault rifle and the RAAL MG.

Tank Battleground is a limited-time multiplayer game mode featured in Call of Duty: Mobile. It was added in January 2025 as part of Season 1: Wings of Vengeance. In Tank Battleground, all players are spawned into the match inside a Tank and must eliminate the other team in standard Team Deathmatch rules.

The Last Train is Chapter 12 and the thirteenth mission in Call of Duty 2: Big Red One. It is the second of the two levels in the game where the player takes control of a tank, but only through part of this level.

The Eder Dam is the eleventh campaign mission in Call of Duty and Call of Duty: Classic. The SAS's objective is to destroy nine anti-aircraft guns, then enter the Eder Dam facility and plant explosives on the electrical generators.

A Technical is an improvised fighting vehicle featured in all of the Modern Warfare installments of the Call of Duty series. It is usually a pickup truck with a mounted machine gun, usually an M2 Browning Machine Gun. Similar vehicles appear in Call of Duty: Black Ops, but are not pick-up trucks, and they instead have the Russian DShk mounted machine gun. The DShK appears in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 as well, but the M2 accompanies it. In Call of Duty: Modern Warfare, it is drivable in the Ground War mode and Spec Ops, but it doesn't have a machine gun in the back.

The Telescopic Sight is a weapon attachment featured in Call of Duty: World at War. It is also available to unique weapons in Call of Duty 3, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, Modern Warfare 2: Ghost and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 Campaign Remastered.

The Teleporter is a utility in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare on the Exo Zombies map Carrier. It costs 100 credits to activate. It serves the exact same purpose as the Trash Chute from previous maps, even sharing the same price.
Tear Gas is a chemical weapon in Call of Duty: Black Ops and Call of Duty: Black Ops II, and an item of tactical equipment that appears in Call of Duty: Ghosts.
Ted Bock is a minor character in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare. In the level "Sentinel", he is driving a truck with Dr. Bellamy in it, who is to see Jonathan Irons.

The Teleport Grenade, is a piece of equipment in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare on the Exo Zombies maps Carrier, from the DLC Pack Supremacy, and Descent, from the DLC Pack Reckoning. The achievement/trophy Telefragathon requires the player to kill fifty zombies with the teleport grenade. The achievement Coast 2 Coast requires the player to cross the water with a teleport grenade.

Terrestrial Ammo is a weapon attachment that appears in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. It is available for the HVR and Rack-9, to which it is an integral attachment. It allows the HVR to achieve three shot kills to the body at close range, making it the only submachine gun capable of killing in three hits in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare without headshots. For the Rack-9, it allows superior stopping power compared to its fellow shotguns.

Tech Savvy is a Legendary gun perk in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. It is current found on the Legendary Atlas - Overwatch variant. It grants the player the perk Engineer when the player is either crouched or prone, as well as when the player is standing still.

The Tesla Gun is a semi-automatic geistkraft weapon featured in the maps The Final Reich, The Shadowed Throne, The Tortured Path, Bodega Cervantes, U.S.S. Mount Olympus, and Altar of Blood within the Nazi Zombies mode of Call of Duty: WWII.

The Den is a carrier and is the home base of the JTF Wolverines. The carrier is rather theoretical and does not pertain to the the setting of the campaign. The interior of the ship is only seen in the mission team cutscene while Commander James Rhomer is introducing you to the whole setup of the team. The interior of the carrier is similar to Retribution, but instead of the SATO logo painted on the wall, it is replaced with the JTF Wolverines logo. It would appear the ship is thus an Admiral-class carrier.

Tempus Armament Inc., sometimes abbreviated as TA, is a weapon manufacturer in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare, Call of Duty: Mobile, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III, and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4. Their logo is a mailed fist holding a spiked mace with a heraldic shield background or simply their abbreviated name, but bold and capitalized.
The is a marksman rifle featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III, and Call of Duty: Black Ops 6.
The Tempered Plate Carrier is an equipment featured in Call of Duty: Warzone 2.0, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II, Call of Duty: Mobile, and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.

The is a bullpup assault rifle featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II. It was added as part of the Season Four update. The Tempus Razorback is also available in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III as part of the Modern Warfare II content carryover.
Tectonic Tactical is a weapon manufacturer in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III.
The Gun Battery is the fifth track of the Call of Duty: Vanguard (Original Game Soundtrack). It is composed by [https://bearmccreary.com Bear McCreary], with a runtime of 3:27.

Terminator may refer to: *Model 1887 - A weapon commonly referred to as Terminator. *Task Force Terminators - A faction featured in Call of Duty: Vanguard. *T-800 - An operator in Call of Duty: Vanguard and Call of Duty: Black Ops 6. *T-1000 - An operator in Call of Duty: Vanguard. *The Terminator - An event in Call of Duty: Black Ops 6.

The (sometimes referred to as the Thompson M1A1) is an American submachine gun that appears in almost every Call of Duty title set in World War II to date (excluding Call of Duty: WWII and Call of Duty: Vanguard, where it is replaced by the M1928), as well as appearing in Call of Duty: Black Ops and Call of Duty Online, and being briefly seen in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2.
The Reichstag is the twenty-sixth and final Call of Duty mission. The 150th Rifle Division must push up to the roof of the Reichstag and raise the victory banner.

The (or PzKpfw VI Ausf. H) is a heavy tank used during World War II. The Tiger I was developed to address the formidable Soviet armor encountered in the initial months of Operation Barbarossa, particularly the T-34.

The is a weapon attachment featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, Call of Duty: Ghosts, Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare, Call of Duty: Black Ops III, Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare, Call of Duty: Black Ops 4, Call of Duty: Mobile and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare. It was also cut from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered. The Thermal scope assists aiming by highlighting enemy heat signatures.

:For similar weapons, see Throwing Knife, Combat Axe, Hell's Retriever, and Axe. The is a Lethal featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops, Call of Duty: Black Ops: Declassified and Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War, and briefly seen in Call of Duty: Mobile.
Tiger is a weapon camouflage skin featured in Call of Duty Black Ops, Call of Duty: Black Ops II, and Call of Duty: Black Ops III.

The Titus-6 is a bullpup Special weapon available for use in the campaign mode of Call of Duty: Black Ops II. It fires three rounds of high explosive flechette projectiles that stick onto surfaces before exploding; it must be reloaded every time it is fired, as each magazine only contains a single three round burst. Switching modes folds down the weapon's sight, disabling ADS, and allows it to instead be used as a shotgun. The shotgun works with a two-round burst with a ten-round magazine, and is highly effective against regular infantry in close quarters.
The Titanium Frame is an attachment for the Riot Shield that appears in Call of Duty: Ghosts. It enables faster melee with the shield, similarly to Melee in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3.
Tiki Camouflage is a weapon camouflage in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare. It is available with the purchase of the Tiki Pack. Tiki Personalization Pack AW.jpg|The Tiki Pack poster.

Thunder Wall is an Alternate Ammo Type/Ammo Mod in Call of Duty: Black Ops III. It gives the weapon a chance to blast zombies in a small radius, similar to the Thundergun, except they are blasted vertically. It has to recharge for approximately 15 seconds before it can be used again. Much like other double-packed upgrades, Thunder Wall will kill groups of zombies with each activation, however it only has a smaller radius due to the nature of how it activates. Before an update, Thunder Wall did not generate any points and did not track kills. This has since been remedied, granting 50 points for each zombie killed and counting kills towards leaderboards as normal.
The Titan is an Atomic Dynamics energy light machine gun in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare.

Lieutenant Tom Szakolczay is an antagonist in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare and member of the Settlement Defense Front. He's assigned to the carrier SDS Centauri. Szakolczay is killed by Nick Reyes in a dogfight during Operation Trace Kill.

Threat Designator is an Epic gun perk in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. It is exclusive to the X-Eon - Warsight variant, where it allows its built-in integrated optics to highlight enemies that have Cold Blooded, Hardwired and Active Camo equipped.
The Tidal is a melee weapon that was added to Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered on the June 27th, 2017 update.
The Tigershark is a light machine gun that was added to Call of Duty: Black Ops 4 with the Operation Spectre Rising update.

The Thunderbolt Sling is a Signature Attachment for the HBRa3 assault rifle in the Stock category. It was added in February 2022 as part of the Season 2: Task Force 141 update. When equipped, the HBRa3 will receive reduced Sprint-to-Fire delay, as well as the improvement of ADS quickness, flinch resistance, recoil control and hipfire accuracy, in exchange of a rather minor ADS movement speed penalty.

The is a melee weapon featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II. It was added as part of the Season Four update. The Tonfa is also available in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III as part of the Modern Warfare II content carryover.
Tiber is a weapon manufacturer featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops 6.

The Thermal 6x is a thermal optic featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops 6. It is classed as a Universal Attachment and unlocking it for the weapon it is unlocked under, unlocks it for the entire weapon class. It is available for Marksman Rifles and Sniper Rifles.

Sergeant Thomas "Tank" Dempsey is a character featured in the Dark Aether Saga of Zombies mode. Dempsey appears in Call of Duty: Black Ops 6 in the ending cutscene of Reckoning and as a canon playable character in all maps of Call of Duty: Black Ops 7. He is also a playable Operator of the JSOC faction in Black Ops 7 Multiplayer and Call of Duty: Warzone 2.0.

Train Station is the seventeenth campaign mission in Call of Duty and Call of Duty: Classic. Corporal Alexei Voronin must push through the train station to tell Major Zubov that Red Square has been recaptured.

The Type 100 is a Japanese submachine gun, featured in Call of Duty: World at War, Call of Duty: Zombies, Call of Duty: World at War (Nintendo DS), Call of Duty: Black Ops, Call of Duty: WWII and Call of Duty: Vanguard.
The was a Japanese light machine gun used by the Imperial Japanese Army during World War II.

The is a medium tank used by the Imperial Japanese Army during World War II and featured in Call of Duty: World at War and Call of Duty: World at War: Final Fronts. The standard [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Type_97_Chi-Ha_medium_tank Type 97 Chi-Ha] appears in the game files of world at War but is unused.
The is a Japanese heavy machine gun that appears in Call of Duty: World at War and Call of Duty: Black Ops.
The ("Triple Type 96 25mm AT/AA Gun") is an anti-aircraft weapon of World War II, featured in the Pacific campaign of Call of Duty: World at War.
The is a small vehicle used by Japanese forces throughout World War II. This vehicle is seen in multiplayer maps on Call of Duty: World at War, such as Hangar.
The , also known as the UAZ-469, is an all-terrain vehicle used by the Ultranationalists, Soviet Armed Forces and Spetsnaz.
Train Bridge is the sixth mission in the Call of Duty: United Offensive campaign.

The Type 95 is a bullpup assault rifle in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, Call of Duty Online and Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War. It was also scheduled to appear in Call of Duty: Black Ops II , but was replaced by the Type 25.
The (Unmanned Ground Vehicle) is a heavily armed vehicle featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 and Call of Duty: Ghosts.

The was an unarmed armored personnel carrier used by the Imperial Japanese Army in World War II. It was set to appear in Call of Duty: World at War but was cut sometime during the development stages. All that remains are texture sheets and two model files: One undestroyed, and one destroyed. The name of the complete model is vehicle_jap_tracked_type1ho-ki_mp. The suffix MP seems to suggest that the vehicle was going to be used in multiplayer.
The Type 25 (called Type 95 in the game files) is a bullpup assault rifle featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops II, Call of Duty: Strike Team and Call of Duty: Mobile.
The Type85 Evolution is a sniper rifle featured in Call of Duty Online. It acts as a replacement for the Dragunov from previous games.

.]] The Tram is a utility featured in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare, in the Zombies mode of Call of Duty: Black Ops III, and a vehicle in V.E.R.S.I.O.N., Call of Duty: Warzone, Call of Duty: Warzone 2.0, Call of Duty: Mobile, and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.

The Type-2 (referred to as the MOD2 in pre-release, and as FMG in the game files) is a Fujiwara hybrid energy assault rifle featured in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare, capable of alternating between an assault rifle mode and a dual wielded machine pistol mode. Its features resemble a submachine gun over an assault rifle, the FMG9 specifically; handling of the weapon behaves as a compromise between an AR and SMG from its mobility and high rate of fire.
The , otherwise known as the SA-15 'Gauntlet, is a mobile surface-to-air (SAM) system capable of shooting down aircraft and UAVs featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2.

The Tracking Chip is an optical attachment that appears in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare, exclusively for all scoped sniper rifles. It modifies a Sniper Rifle scope to highlight targets in a similar way to a Trojan sight. Much like the Trojan sight, the Tracking Chip is countered by the perk Hardwired.

Triad is an Epic gun perk in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. The perk is exclusive to the Bomber, an Epic variant of the EBR-800 sniper rifle. The perk causes the weapon to fire in a charged three round burst.

Twinsanity is an Epic gun perk in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. It allows the weapon to become Akimbo, causing a tighter hip spread and devastating damage up close, at the expense of losing the ability to aim down the sights. It is only available to the HVR - Gemini and Auger - Fury variants. The Auger - Fury variant has a tighter hip spread the longer the weapon is fired.

The Top-Loading Clip is an ammo mechanism featured in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. It is integrated to the DMR-1 sniper rifle and the M1 classic weapon. The DMR-1 can reload at any time unlike the M1, which can only reload by shooting the entire clip.
:For similarly named weapons, see Axe, Ice Axe and Combat Axe. The is a melee weapon featured in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare and Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War.
The Tribal (or Tribal Staff in development) is a melee weapon that was added to Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered in the June 27th, 2017 update.
Trample is a Rare gun perk in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare, found upon certain weapon variants. It adds a large score bonus to the user's Payload upon the achievement of a double kill.

The Trek-50 (known as the Ba50 in the game files) is a single shot sniper rifle that was added to Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare in the June 27th, 2017 update. It is a break-action, high-calibre sniper rifle with strong similiarities to the MORS and RW1 from Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare.

Tri-Barrel is an Epic gun perk in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. It is exclusive to the Epic M.2187 - Salvo variant. It gives the weapon a higher damage range and extra damage on extremities such as the legs and arms.
The is a semi-automatic rifle that appears in Call of Duty: WWII. It was added with the Blitzkrieg event on April 17th 2018.

The is a melee weapon that was added to Call of Duty: WWII with the Winter Siege event. Within Nazi Zombies the Mean Machine variant can be used within The Shadowed Throne where it can be found in the Cabaret and within The Tortured Path along with the accompanied survival maps either from B.A.T Supply Drops or the Mystery Box.
The is a bolt-action sniper rifle that was added to Call of Duty: WWII with the Blitzkrieg event on April 17th, 2018.
The Triumph is a light machine gun featured in Call of Duty Online. It can switch between LMG mode and Akimbo shotgun mode.
The is a semi-automatic rifle appearing as a tactical rifle in Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War and as a marksman rifle in Call of Duty: Mobile.

The Tracker Rifle is an operator skill that was cut from Call of Duty: Mobile. It had a design based off the M4, and would be capable of automatically locking the aim of the weapon onto enemy players, along with a holographic shield on the weapon which would protect the player from hit from the front. It appeared to be played on Chinese Alpha, however after this, It never appeared again and was cut from the game.

The Tranquilizer Gun, or Dart Gun as labeled in the HUD, is a non-lethal handgun featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War. The weapon is only usable in the mission "Brick in the Wall" and is used by Bell during their infiltration of Franz Kraus' apartment to bug his briefcase to gain the location of Anton Volkov.
The is a light machine gun featured in Call of Duty: Vanguard.

The is a submarine in Call of Duty: Vanguard. The ship appears in the campaign mission Phoenix and the Multiplayer map Sub Pens both taking place in Hamburg, Nazi Germany. It was designed by the Kriegsmarine.
Tough is a Weapon Perk featured in Call of Duty: Mobile. It helps by increasing the movement speed of the player by a substantial percentage after respawning, but lasts for a few seconds.
The is a light machine gun featured in Call of Duty: Vanguard. It was added as part of the Season Four update.

The was an anti-tank gun developed by the Imperial Japanese Army, and used in combat during World War II. It was primarily used on Peleliu island defenses to destroy American Sherman Tanks. It is encountered in the levels Hard Landing and Relentless where the player needs to kill there crews. They can be destroyed by the Triple 25 in the latter level.
The is an assault rifle featured in Call of Duty: Mobile. It was added in February 2024 as part of the Season 2: Lunar Dragon update.

Triple Barrel Burst is an Epic gun perk in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. It is exclusive to the "Thunderstruck" Prototype Weapon version of the M.2187. It is a modified version of the Tri-Barrel gun perk, but fires all three barrels in succession. It also disables the use of Akimbo as an attachment on the weapon.

The [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Type_41_75_mm_mountain_gun Type 41 75 mm mountain gun] was a mounted weapon used by the Imperial Japanese Army, and used in combat during World War I and World War II. The Type 41 mountain gun appears at the airfield during the level Numa Numa Trail. The player needs to destroy it with a grenade to stop it from destroying friendly M4 Shermans.

The (Japanese: 九八式臼砲, Hepburn: kyūhachi-shiki-kyūhō), was an artillery weapon used by the Imperial Japanese Army throughout World War II. They appear only in the level Typhoon of Steel in the middle of the level. They are seen firing on the marines positions. The player is tasked with killing the crews.

The Type 104 was a submachine gun that was featured in Call of Duty: Future Warfare. However, when Future Warfare was canceled, the Type 104 was discarded as well, and was never ported to any other future titles.

The Type 207 was a submachine gun that was featured in Call of Duty: Future Warfare. However, when Future Warfare was canceled, the Type 207 was discarded as well, and was never ported to any other future titles. Due to the early stage by which Future Warfare was uncovered, the Type 207's look was not final - as it beared the same look as the Mini-Uzi from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2

Torque may refer to: *Kieran "Torque" Mackay - A Specialist in Call of Duty: Black Ops 4. *Bow - Known as the Torque 35 in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III. *Torque (map) - A map in Call of Duty: Black Ops 7.
The is a light machine gun featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.

Private Travers is one of the men at the camp at Saint Lo. He can be seen walking around the camp. He was in the truck with Dixon, Nichols, Huxley, McCord and Young. He is positioned to the left of Huxley. When the Germans opened fire on the squad, he was shot and as a result he fell off the truck. His fate is unknown although after being shot and falling off a truck, he would have slim chances of survival.
twalker is the user account name of T. Walker on servers accessible from the computer terminal in the interrogation room depicted in the main menu of Call of Duty: Black Ops.

Train Chase is the thirty-second soundtrack in Call of Duty: Ghosts.

Trident may refer to: *Trident 3-1 - A Delta Force callsign in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3. *KL03-Trident - A weapon in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare. *Task Force Trident - A multiplayer faction in Call of Duty: Vanguard. *Mission: Trident - A multiplayer map in Call of Duty: Black Ops 7

Underground Passage is a campaign level in Call of Duty: Finest Hour featuring the Americans in the Battle of Aachen. The player controls Sergeant Chuck Walker who needs to move through the Aachen sewers to reach the center of the city. The main objective is to destroy 5 ladders to prevent the German Army from launching surprise attacks.
The Ural-4320 is a Russian transport truck featured in Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 and Call of Duty: Mobile.

The is a submachine gun featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, Find Makarov, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, Call of Duty Online, Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III. It was cut from Call of Duty: Ghosts.

Urban Camouflage is a vehicle camouflage skin featured in Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare and a weapon camouflage featured in both Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare and Call of Duty: Black Ops 4. This camouflage can also be seen on some Ultranationalist soldiers in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 and preceding games, most likely symbolizing communist ideals. In Multiplayer, it is one of the most common camouflage options seen being unlocked as a camouflage option after acquiring 30 headshots with any primary weapon, yet looking similar to Red Tiger camouflage.

U.S.S. Chicago is a submarine in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2. It was seen in "The Only Easy Day... Was Yesterday". It was part of the Sixth Fleet leading the counterstrike on the oil rig. Captain MacTavish's team, Hotel Six, was launched to the oil rig out of the U.S.S. Chicago and met up with Team Two out of the U.S.S. Dallas.

U.S.S. Dallas is a Los Angeles-class nuclear attack submarine featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2. It appears in "The Only Easy Day... Was Yesterday". It launched Team Two of Hotel Six to the oil rig, shortly after the player departs the U.S.S. Chicago with Team One.

:For other variants, see Mini-Uzi, WSP Stinger and WSP Swarm. The is a submachine gun featured in Modern Warfare 2: Ghost, Call of Duty: Black Ops, Call of Duty: Black Ops II, Call of Duty: Black Ops: Declassified, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III and Call of Duty: Mobile.

The or Bren Gun Carrier is a British family of light-armored tracked vehicles commonly used to transport personnel or to act as a machine gun platform. The Universal Carrier was widely used by the British Army and various Commonwealth forces.
The USS Nimitz (CVN-68) was the lead ship of the Nimitz-class of nuclear-powered aircraft carriers. The Nimitz appears in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3.

The V-22 "Osprey" is a double-turboprop, tilt-rotor aircraft developed for the US Military. The V-22 appears in Find Makarov: Operation Kingfish, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, Call of Duty: Ghosts and in the specialist HQ portion of Call of Duty: Black Ops 4.

:Not to be confused with Arctic Camouflage. The Unknown Arctic Camouflage is an unnamed weapon camouflage that appears in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, in the mission "Cliffhanger". It is only available for the ACR. It is similar to the White Tape Camouflage in the fact that it appears to be a totally makeshift camo, seemingly white strokes of paint applied to the weapon in a stripe/zig-zag like-pattern.
The Unknown Chemical Weapon was a chemical weapon used during World War III as part of Makarov's plan to bring Europe into The Third World War.

VTOL (Vertical Take Off and Landing) refers to several different aircraft in various games which are fixed-wing and use turbofan thrusters mounted on each wing. These VTOLs appear in Call of Duty: Black Ops II, Call of Duty: Strike Team, Call of Duty: Black Ops III, Call of Duty: Mobile and Call of Duty: Black Ops 7. Their main purpose is transportation.
The [http://combatrifle.com/remington-700-usr-urban-sniper-rifle USR] is a sniper rifle that appears in Call of Duty: Ghosts.
The VKS is a bullpup sniper rifle that appears in Call of Duty: Ghosts. It has an integrated silencer like the Honey Badger and K7.

The USS Liberator (CVN-81) was a Gerald R. Ford-class aircraft carrier built and operated by United States Navy in Call of Duty: Ghosts. It first appeared in the cutscene for Sin City and later in the level All or Nothing.

The UK Punk Camouflage is a DLC weapon camouflage skin available for Call of Duty: Black Ops II. It is available for anyone who buys the UK Punk Pack. The camouflage consists of the U.K. flag design on the weapon, and the secondary design is a red and black plad design.
Unicorn Personalization Pack is a downloadable content package available for Call of Duty: Ghosts. It contains a weapon camo, reticle, a player background and a player patch.

The USS Oregon was a Arleigh Burke-class destroyer that appeared in the 15th mission of Call of Duty: Ghosts, "All or Nothing". She was assigned to the carrier group of the USS Liberator and was heavily damaged or capsized in the Southern Atlantic Ocean.

The Unknown Ghillie Camouflage is a weapon camouflage skin seen in Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered. It resembles the Ghillie Suit design seen ingame. Unlike other camouflage patterns, the unknown ghillie camouflage has ghillie wrap on it rather than simply being painted. It is exclusively seen on the M21 in campaign mode. It is only used in the levels "Blackout" and "All Ghillied Up". It can also been seen in "F.N.G." on the weapon racks, but like all other weapons, can't be picked up. In Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered, the unknown ghillie camouflage is available for all sniper rifles in Multiplayer, by means of the Ghillie Weapon Kit.

The VSD-Protoype 9, (also known as the Sniper Drone, or WASP in Manhunt) is a pilotable aerial drone with mounted weapon featured in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare and Call of Duty: Mobile. The VSD is a drone that can be armed with a variety of weapons, ranging from machine guns to sniper weapons. It is also equipped with cloaking technology, allowing it to perform covert ops missions.
Urban Jet Camouflage is a camouflage that appears in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare.

The VTOL Cargo Aircraft is a multiplayer exclusive vehicle that appears in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare. Like the V-22 Osprey, it is a double-turboprop, tilt-rotor vehicle. It only appears on "Bio Lab" as part of the map's dynamic event, and will drop a small building near the B flag containing a Minigun.

The USS Arrowhead is an aircraft carrier that appears in the Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare mission "Armada". The carrier was part of the Third Fleet of the US Navy. The Arrowhead appears to be a Triple-Hulled Designed Battle-Carrier with Railguns on both sides of the Ship.
The VMP is a submachine gun featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops III, Call of Duty: Black Ops 4, Call of Duty: Mobile, and Call of Duty: Black Ops 7.

Staff Sergeant Usef Omar is a character featured in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. He leads the Marines aboard the Retribution. While he doesn't always agree with Nick Reyes, he does have his back in a fight. Omar is all about solving problems with action, and has a personal stake in the war against the SDF, as his family suffered at their hands. He has a brash, outspoken exterior, but his mind is always on the mission and the soldiers under his command. When he first meets E3N, he is incredibly harsh towards him, to the point of ignoring him completely, he soon softens his view towards him and eventually personally requests for E3N to join them on a mission. Omar eventually meets his demise when he tries to save Lee, a civilian worker on the Vesta 3 asteroid station, being scorched to death by a winding solar flash. He leaves behind his wife, Sarah, his son, Noah, and his daughter, Abby.

The UNSA SWC-141 Retribution was an Admiral-class Space Warfare Carrier utilized by the United Nations Space Alliance in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare and Call of Duty: Siege. Prior to Geneva, the Retribution and its flotilla were ambushed by an SDF Supercarrier and a squadron of Skelters as they were performing diagnostics on the ships for damage repair from the destruction of a satellite, and were rescued after an intense dogfight involving SCAR 2-1. While the Retribution was present at the Fleet Week Parade at Geneva, it was not supplied prior to the SDF attack. Thus, while it survived the attack, it was not ready for deployment in war. Lieutenant Nick Reyes was promoted to Commanding Officer and made acting captain by Admiral Fredrick Raines after the death of Captain Alder after giving the order for the Retribution to ram the SDF Olympus Mons. Of the 767 officers and crew attacking the SDF Shipyard, only four survived: Nora Salter, Erwin Kloos, Evelynn "Boats" Sotomura and Sean Brooks.

The UNSA Eclipse is a United Nations Space Alliance Zulu-Class DDX Guided Missile Destroyer in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. The warship was built in Saitama, Japan before being put into service under the United Nations Space Alliance Navy. She was present at the Fleet Week Parade and flew directly over Solar Associated Treaty Organization headquarters as it was introduced by the announcer. During the attack on Geneva, the Eclipse provided fire support to the SATO ground troop that retook the AATIS control tower before engaging the Settlement Defense Front fleet in Earth's low orbit with the remains of the UNSA fleet. Unfortunately, she was obliterated, along with several other UNSA destroyers, when the SDS Olympus Mons suddenly appeared out of slipspace.

The UNSA Ocana is a United Nations Space Alliance destroyer. The Ocana was one of the ships to survive the Olympus Mons attack above the Earth. The warship was later destroyed near Neptune by the SDS Galaxius. The remains of the destroyer are seen during Operation Taken Dagger.
The UNSA Nova is a United Nations Space Alliance destroyer. The warship is shot down by the Earth AATIS guns during the attack of Geneva and crashed in the city creating a massive explosion.
The UNSA Endurance is a United Nations Space Alliance destroyer. The warship is shot down by the Earth AATIS guns during the attack of Geneva and crashed into the lake causing a tidal wave.

The UNSA Vengeance is a United Nations Space Alliance destroyer and was the personal ship of Admiral Fredrick Raines. The warship is shot down by the Earth AATIS guns hacked by the Settlement Defense Front during the attack of Geneva, although without Raines onboard.

The VPR (known as Hades in pre-release) is a Kendall Ballistics fully-automatic double barreled submachine gun featured in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare that was added in the March 28th, 2017 update. It looks similar to the MP5K from previous games in many ways, such as the iron sights and silhouette of the weapon, though the weapon now has two barrels and differently mounted magazines. It is available for free for Season Pass holders, otherwise it can be unlocked via a challenge or a Supply Drop (acquire any variant).
The VRAP is a vehicle featured in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare. It is a futuristic MRAP that is extensively used by Atlas as their counter to the Pitbull.
The UNSA Tunguska is a United Nations Space Alliance destroyer, and one of the best in the fleet. The warship was destroyed by the Settlement Defense Front during the attack on Geneva.

The VAPR-XKG is an assault rifle featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops 4. It was developed in the United States by the fictional manufacturer LVWS Phantom. It also has an MKII variant along with a Mastercraft variant.

The UNSA Icarus 03 was a United Nations Space Alliance frigate made by the United States, Mexico, Japan and the United Kingdom. The ship was last seen falling into a black hole known as Cygnus X-3. It was disintegrated by the strong gravitational field around the massive astronomical entity. It is featured on the multiplayer map Mayday. From what little can be seen, the frigate seems to resemble destroyers such as UNSA Tigris and the UNSA Eclipse, at least with regards to its dorsal thrusters and rear. It is unclear exactly how the ship managed to get to Cygnus X-3, a real life black hole that is 23,480 light years from Earth, given that FTL ships in Infinite Warfare seem to suffer substantial stress for FTL jumps over the relatively short distance of the Solar System.
The is a light machine gun that was added in Call of Duty: WWII with the Shadow War update.
The VKM 750 is a light machine gun featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops 4. It has high damage and doesn't deal less damage at long range, but its fire rate is extremely low.
UNSA Cruisers are a type of warship that appear in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. They are also seen in the sky of the Black Sky mission.

The VTOL ("Vertical Take-Off and Landing") Jet is a Killstreak featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare, a Killstreak and Scorestreak in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III, and a Scorestreak in Call of Duty: Mobile.
VLK (Cyrillic: ВЛК) is a weapon manufacturer in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III.
The VTOL Drone is an aircraft that appears in Call of Duty: Black Ops III. It first appears in mission Black Ops.

The VTOL Cargo Plane is a vehicle that appears in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare. It is a futuristic cargo aircraft with the ability to take off and land vertically. It is used by both the United States of America and Atlas Corporation. It makes an appearance in Call of Duty: Mobile.

UNSA Destroyers are a type of warship that appear in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare, under the command of the United Nations Space Alliance and its military arm, the Solar Associated Treaty Organization.
The is a Scorestreak featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War. Unlike the VTOL Jet or Harrier Strike of previous games, this version of the VTOL streak is player-controlled.

The Utility Truck is a ground vehicle featured in Call of Duty: Warzone. It was added as part of the Season One update of Call of Duty: Vanguard. It is only available in Caldera. It is very similar to the Cargo Truck and Armored Truck.
The is an aircraft carrier featured in Call of Duty: Vanguard. Part of the United States Navy, the ship can be seen during the mission The Battle of Midway with Wade Jackson stationed aboard.
The is an aircraft carrier featured in Call of Duty: Vanguard. Part of the United States Navy, the ship can be seen during the mission The Battle of Midway, sailing along its sister ship Enterprise.

The is a vehicle featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III. In Modern Warfare II and Modern Warfare III, the UTV is available for use in Multiplayer in the Ground War and Invasion game modes and in the DMZ mode. In Modern Warfare III, it is available for use in the Zombies mode on the experience Operation Deadbolt.

"Usenko" Amory Plant (ukr. Збройовий Завод "Усенко") or Usenko (ukr. Усенко) is a weapon manufacturer in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III, Call of Duty: Warzone Mobile.

The VMF Variable Scope is a variable optic featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops 6. It is classed as a Universal Attachment and unlocking it for the weapon it is unlocked under, unlocks it for the entire weapon class. It is available for SMGs, LMGs, Marksman Rifles and Sniper Rifles.
The VS Recon is a bullpup sniper rifle featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops 7.
The VST is a submachine gun featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops 7. It was added as part of the Season Three update.
The VX Compact is a bullpup assault rifle featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops 7. It was added on June 11th, 2026 as part of the Season Four update.
Usurped Flame is a resource and weapon featured in the Call of Duty: Black Ops 7 Zombies map Rex Infernus. It, and it's upgraded variant Astral Flame, are primarily used as a quest mechanic.

*USSR - Abbreviated name for Soviet Russia *​USS Barack Obama - An Aircraft carrier that appear in Call of Duty: Black Ops II *​USS Liberator - An aircraft carrier that appears in Call of Duty: Ghosts *​USS Carolina - A Destroyer that appears in Call of Duty: Ghosts *​USS Chicago - A Submarine that appears in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 **​USS Dallas - Another Submarine that appears in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 *USS Texas - A New York-class battleship appears as a multiplayer map in Call of Duty: WWII

Vehicle challenges are a category of challenge in Call of Duty: World at War. They're progressively unlocked from level 23 and to complete them the player must undertake a variety of tasks that involve the tanks found in certain multiplayer levels. These levels include: *Downfall *Outskirts *Seelow *Roundhouse

The is a bullpup, semi-automatic sniper rifle featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, Call of Duty: Black Ops, Call of Duty Online, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III. It was cut from Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3.

The Väljakutse (also known as the Estonian Freighter) is a cargo ship that appears in the mission Crew Expendable in Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered, where it is infiltrated by the Special Air Service in order to obtain a "package" located in the hold of the ship. The ship is later sunk by several missiles launched from a couple Ultranationalist MiG-29 fighter jets. A modified version of the ship appears in the multiplayer map, Wet Work, and the ship's model is later reused in the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 Special Ops mission Suspension.

Vorschlaghammer (German for Sledgehammer) is a Leopard 2 battle tank of the Bundeswehr and appears in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3. Vorschlaghammer appears in the mission "Scorched Earth", which takes place in Berlin, Germany.
Vulture 2-2 is an MH-6 Little Bird used during the Special Ops mission Little Bros. It is piloted by Colonel Munson and has a marksman, Sergeant Hammer, on one of its skids.

The is a submachine gun featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, Call of Duty: Black Ops II, Call of Duty: Strike Team, Call of Duty: Ghosts, Call of Duty Online, Call of Duty: Heroes, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare, Call of Duty: Mobile, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III. It was also seen in early trailers of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, but was cut from the final product.

The is a British-designed gas operated machine gun that appeared in the Call of Duty 3 Campaign. Sets of Vickers K machine guns are seen mounted on Vera and Lynn. The player uses two twin-linked Vickers K machine guns briefly in the mission Hostage!. They are very powerful, but somewhat inaccurate further made difficult with the movement of the vehicles.
The Viper Camouflage is a DLC weapon camouflage skin for Call of Duty: Black Ops II. It is available for anyone who buys the Viper Pack for 160 MS Points or for $1.99 USD on PSN.
The Vepr is a bullpup submachine gun that appears in Call of Duty: Ghosts and Call of Duty Online.

The Venom-X is a special projectile weapon that shoots either acid puddles, fire (Venom-FX), lightning (Venom-LX) or friendly Seeder turrets (Venom-SX), introduced in the Onslaught DLC for Call of Duty: Ghosts, being featured in the Nightfall, Mayday, and Awakening chapters of Extinction. It also appears as an easter egg in the Unearthed map included in the Devastation DLC. The Venom-X later returns in the Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare zombies map The Beast From Beyond and later was added to multiplayer as part of the September 26th, 2017 update.
The Vesper is a bullpup submachine gun featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops III.

Vehicular Combat is a mechanic featured in many games of the Call of Duty series. It allows the player to make use of a vehicle to fight enemies in similar means or to take out hardened targets with either limited or, in some cases, full control of their craft.

Visor Detonation is a Legendary gun perk in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. Headshot kills will cause an explosion which will damage or kill nearby enemies. This has a similar affect against Zombies in Zombies Mode.

The Vlad, also called Harpoon Gun, is a wonder weapon in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare, introduced in the Zombies map Rave in the Redwoods. The Vlad itself is an explosive tip crossbow, but it can be upgraded into four more powerful variants.
Vanish is an Legendary gun perk in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. It grants the player Blind Eye while they are in prone while holding the Prototype Weapon in question.
The is an automatic rifle featured in Call of Duty: WWII and Call of Duty: Vanguard.

Verdansk Arms Plant (Russian: Верданский Оружейный Завод) is a weapon manufacturer in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III. Their logo is a capital B within a circle with a bullet passing through the upper portion of the B.

The Vodianoy is ship featured in Call of Duty: Warzone. First seen on Rebirth Island during Season One of Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War, the ship disappeared from Rebirth and was seen visible near the coast of Verdansk under a massive thunderstorm. With the release of Season Two, the Vodianoy became a new major point of interest within Verdansk, as Zone 5F. It was removed during Season Three with the launch of Verdansk '84.

Vehicle Horns are a vehicle customization featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare, Call of Duty: Warzone and Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War. In Modern Warfare, Vehicle Horns were added with the Season Four update, and in Black Ops Cold War, available at launch.. Vehicle Horns are mostly store-only items bought through in-game currencies.

Vital is a weapon proficiency in Call of Duty: Vanguard and Call of Duty: Warzone available for the STG44, ITRA Burst, Cooper Carbine, Type 100, Combat Shotgun, Double Barrel, M1 Garand, SVT-40, M1916, Type 99, and 1911. It increases the area of which bullets can do the same amount of damage on an enemy as a headshot, however, this is not the case when paired against larger-caliber ammunition. In Call of Duty: Warzone, it increases torso damage rather than the area for critical hit damage, but increases overall recoil and reduces accuracy.

The Vioxy DX5 is an American SUV made by the car company Vioxy. It is featured in Modern Warfare 2, Modern Warfare 3 and Black Ops 2. It's mostly used as props and scenery, but a militarized version is seen being used by the Shadow Company and Ultranationalists in the Modern Warfare series and seen used by the Navy SEALs in Black Ops 2. It is seen in various colors but its mostly seen in black. The car is based on a 2007 Cadillac Escalade ESV.
The is an assault rifle featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War, Call of Duty: Vanguard, and Call of Duty: Mobile.
The is a submachine gun featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III.
Vertical Recoil Control is a weapon mod featured in the Battle Royale mode of Call of Duty: Mobile.
:For other variants, see Uzi, Mini-Uzi and WSP Stinger. The is a submachine gun featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III.
WSP is a weapon manufacturer in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III. Their logo is the same as their name, with a stylized P.

The WSP Akimbo Brace Stock is a conversion kit for the WSP Swarm submachine gun featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III as part of the Aftermarket Parts system. It was added on the November 22nd, 2023 update. It decreases hipfire spread to near pinpoint accuracy and weapon swap speed in exchange for raw damage, fire-rate, and movement speed.

The Void Cannon Trap is a utility featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops 6 Zombies map, Terminus. It is a trap that when purchased for 1750 Essence, will lift Zombie types into a void, killing them. The trap can also lift the player into it, teleporting them to a different part of the map.
The Voyak KT-3 is a bullpup assault rifle featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops 7. It was added on March 12th, 2026 as part of the Season Two Reloaded update.

The Void Claw is a piece of Tactical Wonder Weapon equipment featured in Call of Duty: Black Ops 7 Zombies in the map Rex Infernus. It is a Grappling Hook type device that allows the player to quickly traverse the map.

Vulcan may refer to: *M61 Vulcan Cannon - A mounted weapon in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2, Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, and Call of Duty: Ghosts. *XS1 Vulcan - A scorestreak in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare. *XR-3 Ion Vulcan Minigun - An attachment in Call of Duty: Black Ops 7. *KG-7 Vulcan - A sniper rifle in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4.
Warsaw Railyard is the twenty-first campaign mission in Call of Duty and Call of Duty: Classic. After securing the tank facility, Sergeant Voronin must exit the factory complex.

Warsaw Factory is the twentieth campaign mission in Call of Duty and Call of Duty: Classic. The 150th Rifle Division must capture a facility in Warsaw, Poland, before the main invasion force can arrive.

Water Cooler is a Vehicle Perk in [http://callofduty.wikia.com/wiki/Call_of_Duty:_World_at_War Call of Duty: World at War] that decreases turret overheat by 30%. This perk is usually deemed useless to the MG gunner as the fire button can simply be rapidly tapped to decrease turret overheat.
Private Webb is a soldier of Able Company under the command of Lt. Walker in Call of Duty: Finest Hour. He is seen in the campaign level "Last Bridge Standing".

Second Lieutenant Walker was one of the few Lieutenants seen in Call of Duty 3 with the American forces. He first appears in the level The Crossroads when Walker is in melee attack with a German in a blown up room. Lieutenant Walker can die at any time but sometimes plays a roll in a cut scene. Lieutenant Walker is also seen making gestures to his men so they will storm a house on the level The Island. Unfortunately, Lieutenant Walker is cut down by a German MP-40 along with two other soldiers.
The Walther G41 is a semi-automatic rifle featured in Call of Duty: World at War (Nintendo DS).

in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2.]] Weapon Camouflage, usually referred to as Camo, is a colored pattern applied to weapons to allow them to blend in to environments, although it is more often used for players to "show off" their achievements in-game as in Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2 camouflages are unlocked by Headshots. In Call of Duty: Black Ops, camouflages can be purchased for each, with the exception of Gold Camouflage, which costs and is available only after the player has Prestiged 14 times. In Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3, weapon camouflage is achieved by increasing the weapon level of a weapon. In Call of Duty: Black Ops II, Call of Duty: Black Ops III and Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered, they are achieved mostly through headshots, one-shot kills or aircraft destroyed depending on the weapon type. After the camouflages that require the aforementioned, there are different challenges to unlock them, such as killing a certain amount of enemies with no perks equipped. The White Tape Camouflage is a weapon camouflage skin consisting of strips of white tape stuck diagonally to a weapon. It is featured only in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2s campaign and special ops modes, and exclusively on the FAMAS. The White Tape camouflage is seen in the campaign levels, "Cliffhanger", "The Only Easy Day... Was Yesterday", "The Gulag", "Contingency", and "Museum", as well as the Special Ops missions "Evasion", "Acceptable Losses", "Sniper Fi", and "Wetwork". This camouflage is only used by Ultranationalist forces. Considering the weather conditions in the levels in which this camouflage appears, it is considered an improvised Arctic Camouflage.
Warsaw Camouflage is a weapon camouflage in Call of Duty: Black Ops.
Weapon Proficiencies are a type of weapon customization featured in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 3 and Call of Duty: Vanguard.
Weight Balance is an attachment in Call of Duty: Black Ops: Declassified. It decreases the recoil of the gun it is used on, similarly to the Grip from other Call of Duty installments.
The Weapon Locker is a utility featured in the Zombies mode of Call of Duty: Black Ops II. It appears in TranZit, Die Rise and Buried.

The Weapon Specialist is a class in Extinction Mode for Call of Duty: Ghosts. Weapon Specialists receive weapon handling and damage improvements to make them the most adept at killing cryptids. By default, all bullet weapons will deal twenty percent extra damage for all weapon specialists. Further upgrading the class will speed up aim down sight times, weapon swapping, strafe speeds, and increase damage even further. The Weapon Specialist class confers many of the same benefits as Team Booster, improving aim down sight times, strafe speeds, weapon switch speeds, equipment use speed, and hip-fire spread. The only benefits of Team Booster that elude the Weapon Specialist are the melee swing speed bonus and the objective repair speed bonus. A Weapon Specialist's handling bonuses do not stack with Team Booster effects. The Specialist Upgrade for the Weapon Specialist will grant the user bottomless magazines for a brief period of time, while also increasing damage, increasing the damage of nearby teammates, and when the upgrade is done, the user's magazine will be topped up for free, essentially giving a free magazine of ammo and a free reload. The Weapon Specialist's damage bonus is completely ignored if the Weapon Specialist is using Explosive Ammo or Cryptid Slayer Ammo. The explosive component of these ammo types has a flat 10% damage boost that completely ignores and overrides the Weapon Specialist's damage boost if the Weapon Specialist is using either type of ammo.

Weapon Facility is an achievement/trophy in Call of Duty: Ghosts gamemode Extinction. It is found in the map Nightfall in the Onslaught DLC. It requires the player to gain access to the Facility in Nightfall.
The War Cry Camouflage is a weapon camouflage featured in Call of Duty: Ghosts. It can be earned in multiplayer by winning a clan war in the diamond division.

The Weapon Specialist Upgrade is a bonus pickup featured in Call of Duty: Ghosts in Chaos Mode that is also purchasable from the Armory. Once picked-up and used, the player will have infinite ammo and will also have increased bullet damage. The Weapon Specialist Upgrade is incredibly useful to activate when dealing with Barrier Hives, as it can allow users to lay a ton of damage into a hive without wasting ammo, speeding up the process of clearing the Barrier Hive. When used, the Weapon Specialist Upgrade, when it expires, will leave a full magazine in whatever weapon the user is currently using when the Weapon Specialist Upgrade expires, regardless of how many bullets were in the weapon when the Weapon Specialist Upgrade was used. This can be manipulated to get free ammo and a free reload. This is especially useful for LMGs, which have lots of ammunition and terribly slow reloads. This can be best exploited by activating the Weapon Specialist Upgrade just as a weapon is on the verge of running out of ammo in a long magazine. The Weapon Specialist Upgrade can make the Weapon Specialist user less dependent on ammo drops from allies. The Weapon Specialist Upgrade is also devastating when used for a semi-automatic shotgun, allowing the user to lay down a tremendous amount of firepower without fear of the magazine running dry. The XH9 Warbird is an aircraft featured in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare, Call of Duty: Heroes and Call of Duty: Mobile

Weapons Free is a perk in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare exclusive to Exo Survival mode. It allows players to purchase any weapon from any weapon class (as long as the player has passed the required round to unlock those weapons) from the Weapon Upgrade armory. It will only start appearing in Orbital Care Packages once round 14 is completed, in order to prevent players from having versatile combinations earlier on.

Walker Tanks is an map-based scorestreak that players can get off the Orbital Care Package. This reward is exclusive to the map Comeback. When activated, two T-600 Titans will appear on opposite sides of the map. They will fire lock-on missiles into the air onto the map like mortars, targeting enemy players they detect. Every single kill it gets will result in 25 scorestreak and the kills will count as Assault Drone kills. It is possible to have two pairs of Tanks active simultaneously. Walker Tanks can target and kill people that have Blind Eye.

Weapon Variant Stats are a feature in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare which saw the introduction of multiple weapon variants of a single weapon. These variants, for the most part, have changes in their stats that from the base weapon. The following are the effects of the changes on the weapon variants.

The Weapon Disposal Machine is a utility in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare on the Exo Zombies map Carrier. Located within the Armory location, it is normally inoperable as it requires a hidden Power Generator located in the Cargo Deck, behind Chompy and requiring Teleport Grenades. Turning this Power Generator on will also upgrade the Grenade Disposal Machine and is a required step of the map Easter Egg, Flotsam & Jetsam. When powered, a zombified arm will stick out from the input slot and will react when a hero goes near. Interacting will cause their currently equipped weapon to be given to given to the arm and taken into the machine, where it will return with parts for the Fishing Pole, C4, a bottle of alcohol or credits. The arm will always then emote with a wave or a hang-ten afterwards. The Weapon Disposal Machine cannot take the final weapon a hero processes.

The Water Trap is a utility in Call of Duty: Advanced Warfare on the Exo Zombies map Carrier. When activated, the glass floor of the cage room will release small geysers of water, killing zombies that walk over them, or are hit by them initially.

Weapon Kits, also known as Weapon Build Kits and Zombies Builds, are a feature in the Zombies mode of Call of Duty: Black Ops III, Call of Duty: Black Ops 4, Call of Duty: Black Ops 6, and Call of Duty: Black Ops 7, the Zombies mode of Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare and the Nazi Zombies mode of Call of Duty: WWII.

Weapon Charms (or Accessories) are a weapon customization feature introduced in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare, and have been present in every main title since. Weapon charms function as ornaments adorned on the weapon that react to the physics of a player's movement. Charms are generally earned through microtransactions or the completion of challenges and progression elements in the game. Only one weapon charm can be applied to a weapon at any given time.

Whirlwind is an Epic gun perk in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare. It changes the firing mode of a burst firing weapon into auto-burst, which means it fires in bursts without needing to let go of the trigger. However, the auto-burst firing change increases recoil towards the weapon. It is exclusive to the Hailstorm - Thunder variant.

Weapon Upgrades is a power-up featured in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare Zombies mode. It converts all weapons that have not been Pack-a-Punched that are being held by the players into their Pack-a-Punched versions for free. Weapon Upgrades is by far the rarest out of the power-ups featured in the game. Weapon Upgrades can be identified by a green pistol with an arrow next to it. Unlike other power-ups, Weapon Upgrades cannot be forcefully spawned by a Fate and Fortune Card.

The Whiteout Weapon Kit is a weapon kit in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered It is available for all the Submachine Guns in the game (MP5, Skorpion, Mini-Uzi, AK-74u and P90). It consists of a black and white design; any SMG that has wood on it has the wood replaced with black.
The Waffe 28 (referred to as MP28 in the game files) is a fully-automatic submachine gun featured in Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare and Call of Duty: WWII.
The Warfighter Weapon Kit is a Bounty weapon kit available in Call of Duty: Modern Warfare Remastered.

Weapon Inspection is a feature present in several Call of Duty games. This feature allows the player to inspect the current weapon, offering a better view of the variant, camouflage and current modifications to the weapon. It is not available for some weapons, and it cannot be used entirely in some game modes. During the animation, the player can still fire, reload or aim the weapon to prematurely cancel the inspection.
